title: introduce-retry-hint-header-and-machine-readable-error-envelope-for-openai-compat
author: Ethan Chen
description: Background: customers integrating via the OpenAI-compatible shim need clearer, machine-readable guidance for retry/backoff and consistent error payloads across both streaming and non-streaming endpoints. Motivation: avoid brittle client heuristics (parsing Retry-After heuristically), reduce duplicated logic in SDKs, and make function/tool-calling failure modes explicit so callers can safely decide whether to retry or surface errors to users. What this PR does: 1) Adds a stable response header X-Redwood-Retry-Hint that encodes a short, opaque backoff hint (RFC-safe token) and an optional suggested backoff in seconds (e.g. "t=10;token=abc123"). 2) Introduces a compact, machine-readable error envelope for OpenAI-compat routes: top-level fields error.code, error.message, error.retryable (boolean), error.hints (array of strings). This is emitted for 4xx/5xx and runtime tool-call failures. 3) Normalizes 429/503 classification: 429 => quota/rate-window, 503 => transient capacity/maintenance; both can include the header but different retryable flags. 4) Adds a streaming preamble event for streamed function/tool-call errors so clients receive a structured terminal frame ("event": "error", payload: error envelope) before the stream closes. 5) Updates SDK compatibility notes and docs with examples and guidance (Python/TS snippets) and a migration guide. Checklist: - [x] RFC implemented (link: https://linear.app/ENG/issue/ENG-1481/retry-hint-header-rfc) - [x] Unit + integration tests for header parsing and error envelope - [x] SDK examples updated - [x] E2E smoke on hosted API - [x] Docs + changelog entry Compatibility notes: header is additive and optional; existing clients will continue to work but can opt in to reading X-Redwood-Retry-Hint and the structured error body. See linked linear tasks for further rollout automation.

review_comments: Lena Fischer (2024-11-09): Overall looks good. Need to confirm header format won't conflict with proxies. Suggest switching to an ABNF-safe token and adding validation at ingress.
Ethan Chen (2024-11-09): Responded—using token base64url without padding; added validation in handler and unit tests.
Ravi Kumar (2024-11-10): Can you clarify semantics of error.retryable for streamed tool failures? If a function call fails due to user code, should retryable be false?
Ethan Chen (2024-11-10): Answered—function runtime errors (user code) are not retryable; infrastructure timeouts are retryable. Added mapping table in comments and tests.
Asha Romero (2024-11-12): Please add a short note in the console docs about how retry-hint tokens are rotated/invalidated when capacity changes.
Ethan Chen (2024-11-12): Added docs section and metric to track token churn as requested.
release_notes: Added X-Redwood-Retry-Hint header (opaque token + suggested backoff) and a machine-readable error envelope (error.code, error.message, error.retryable, error.hints). Streaming now emits a terminal structured error frame for tool/function-call failures. This enables SDKs and clients to make deterministic retry decisions.
